promotedOrAdded.name: Ford Motor Company
promotedOrAdded.theme: Battery energy storage systems + data-centre/grid storage
promotedOrAdded.thesis: Ford Energy creates a genuine second infrastructure engine inside Ford: U.S.-assembled LFP battery energy storage systems for utilities, data centres and large industrial customers. The attraction is the reuse of existing battery manufacturing capacity and a bankable industrial balance sheet, but the parent remains dominated by autos.
promotedOrAdded.catalysts: Ford Energy production ramp from late 2027, execution on the EDF framework for up to 20 GWh over five years, additional hyperscaler/utility contracts, domestic-content advantages and proof that storage can absorb underutilised battery capacity at attractive returns.
promotedOrAdded.risks: Auto-cycle exposure, Ford Energy still being immaterial versus the parent, execution risk on the Kentucky conversion, storage pricing competition, battery input costs and capital intensity.
promotedOrAdded.valuationTechnical: Treat Ford as a crossover rather than a clean BESS pure play. The stock should not receive a data-centre/storage multiple until Ford Energy demonstrates material revenue, backlog and margins.
promotedOrAdded.researchNote: Ford formally launched Ford Energy as a wholly owned subsidiary serving utilities, data centres and industrial customers, targeting at least 20 GWh of annual deployment. A five-year framework allows EDF power solutions North America to procure up to 4 GWh annually, or 20 GWh total, with deliveries expected from 2028.

promotedOrAdded.name: Merck & Co.
promotedOrAdded.thesis: Merck combines an established oncology franchise with optionality from personalized mRNA cancer vaccines through its Moderna partnership, giving a lower-risk way to participate in the platform than owning only the biotech developer.
promotedOrAdded.catalysts: Full Phase 3 melanoma data, regulatory submissions, expansion into additional tumour types and continued Keytruda franchise cash generation.
promotedOrAdded.risks: Keytruda concentration and patent-cycle risk, vaccine regulatory uncertainty, trial-to-commercial translation risk and pipeline execution.
promotedOrAdded.researchNote: Merck and Moderna reported positive Phase 3 melanoma recurrence/metastasis results for personalized mRNA therapy intismeran combined with Keytruda. Detailed data and regulatory follow-up remain important next tests.

promotedOrAdded.name: Moderna
promotedOrAdded.thesis: Positive late-stage melanoma results materially strengthen Moderna's non-COVID platform thesis and validate personalized mRNA oncology as a potential new commercial franchise, but the stock remains binary and pipeline-dependent.
promotedOrAdded.catalysts: Detailed Phase 3 melanoma data, regulatory engagement, additional tumour readouts, commercialization economics with Merck and evidence the platform generalises beyond one cancer setting.
promotedOrAdded.risks: Extremely event-driven valuation, cash burn, incomplete published Phase 3 detail, regulatory risk and uncertainty over addressable population/pricing.
promotedOrAdded.researchNote: The transcript mislabels the ticker as MOA; the company is Moderna (MRNA). The recent price explosion is not itself evidence. The investable change is the positive late-stage melanoma result with Merck, which now requires scrutiny of full efficacy, safety and commercial data.

promotedOrAdded.name: Hims & Hers Health
promotedOrAdded.theme: Consumer metabolic care + weight management + telehealth distribution
promotedOrAdded.thesis: Hims & Hers is a distribution/access layer for consumer metabolic and weight-management care rather than a drug innovator. It can benefit from rising chronic-disease treatment demand, but provider economics, regulation and intense competition make it a higher-risk complement to LLY/DXCM rather than a replacement.
promotedOrAdded.catalysts: Weight-loss membership growth, international expansion, Eucalyptus integration, higher-value personalized plans and successful AI-enabled care workflows.
promotedOrAdded.risks: Regulatory risk around compounded/generic therapies, margin compression, customer acquisition costs, dependence on third-party drug supply and intense telehealth competition.
promotedOrAdded.researchNote: Q1 2026 revenue was $608m, subscribers nearly 2.6m and free cash flow $53m, but U.S. revenue declined and gross margin compressed. Keep below LLY/DXCM until the post-GLP-1 model demonstrates stronger durable unit economics.

promotedOrAdded.name: First Majestic Silver
promotedOrAdded.thesis: First Majestic provides high operating leverage to silver, which benefits from both monetary demand and industrial/electrification uses. It is a much higher-beta expression than owning the metal itself and should be sized accordingly.
promotedOrAdded.catalysts: Sustained silver prices, production growth, Santa Elena development, stronger free cash flow and continued balance-sheet improvement.
promotedOrAdded.risks: Silver-price sensitivity, Mexico jurisdiction concentration, cost inflation, mine execution and sharp drawdowns if precious-metals momentum reverses.
promotedOrAdded.researchNote: Q2 2026 revenue rose 57% to $415.5m, adjusted EBITDA 105% to $257.1m and free cash flow 150% to $194.6m, though AISC rose 22%. Strong numbers justify a tactical watch, but this remains commodity beta rather than a core infrastructure compounder.
